API checks are fast — a health check answers in a millisecond. That speed is a
strategy: run a small, tagged **smoke** check first, and you learn in a second
whether the service is even up before committing to the slow suites.

Close Part 3 with a fast, tagged API health check.

## Task 1 — Tag a fast API health check as smoke

**Goal:** create `checks/speed.robot` with one `smoke`-tagged test that GETs the
health endpoint and asserts a `200`.

Here is the same tagged, fast check against a different endpoint. Adapt it to the
health endpoint.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library     RequestsLibrary
Resource    ../resources/api.resource

*** Test Cases ***
Catalog Smoke
    [Tags]    smoke
    ${resp}=    GET    ${API_URL}/api/products
    Status Should Be    200    ${resp}
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** `Api Smoke` carries the `smoke` tag.

<!-- hint -->
Give the test a `[Tags]    smoke` line as its first step so `--include smoke`
selects it.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Hit the health endpoint: `GET    ${API_URL}/api/health`, then
`Status Should Be    200    ${resp}`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library     RequestsLibrary
Resource    ../resources/api.resource

*** Test Cases ***
Api Smoke
    [Tags]    smoke
    ${resp}=    GET    ${API_URL}/api/health
    Status Should Be    200    ${resp}
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run only the smoke tests

Filter the run to the smoke tag:

```bash
uv run robot --include smoke checks
```

**Check:** the API smoke test passes.
